rankings.blurb: Four Cornerstones including Jahmyr Gibbs, Drake Maye, Puka Nacua, and Trey McBride — this roster is absolutely suffocating. Yes, they overpaid for Gibbs relative to KTC, but when your consolation prize for 'losing' a trade is still Jahmyr freaking Gibbs, you're doing just fine. The cupboard isn't barren either — Cam Ward and Tetairoa McMillan give them real upside beyond the top four. The only knock is just one first-round pick, but when your starters look like this, you don't need to rebuild — you need to win NOW.

Eleven Cornerstones and Foundational players — ELEVEN — which means Sven is basically running a dynasty museum of elite assets while everyone else is shopping at a flea market. Ja'Marr Chase, JSN, Jayden Daniels, Drake London, De'Von Achane, and Omarion Hampton on the same roster is genuinely obscene. The trade record is rough lately and the TE room is a legitimate liability, but this team is so top-heavy with talent that it almost doesn't matter. Sven is one Colston Loveland breakout away from being untouchable.

Seven first-round picks and a roster headlined by Caleb Williams, Jeremiyah Love, and Jaxson Dart — Siny is playing dynasty chess while half this league is playing checkers. The recent trade flipping Breece Hall and late picks for two mid-firsts was sharp work, and dumping Trey McBride at peak value for a haul of picks was a masterclass in dynasty asset management. The current starters are thin on proven NFL production — Love and Dart haven't taken a regular season snap — but the trajectory here is absolutely elite. This team is going to be a monster in 2-3 years, and frankly, it might not take that long.

Josh Allen at 9,998 KTC is the kind of cornerstone that makes other owners physically ill, and pairing him with Ashton Jeanty is an absolute flex. The WR room with Garrett Wilson, Zay Flowers, and Jaylen Waddle is quietly one of the deeper groups in the league, even if none of them are Chase or JSN. The TE position is where this roster quietly bleeds — Sam LaPorta and Kenyon Sadiq are not exactly striking fear into anyone. Gavin's recent trade giving up a first for Baker Mayfield back in a roundabout way wasn't great, but the foundation here is legitimately strong enough to overcome a few bad deals.

Zero first-round picks. ZERO. After getting absolutely smoked by nchernandez19 in a trade that cost them Jameson Williams and two 2029 firsts for Malik Willis and Michael Wilson — a trade so bad it deserves its own Wikipedia page — this team is dangerously thin on future capital. Burrow, Hurts, and Amon-Ra St. Brown make this a legitimate contender right now, but the aging RB room of Jonathan Taylor, Kenneth Walker, and Breece Hall is a walking injury report waiting to happen. This team is one bad season away from a full crisis with no picks to bail them out.

Bijan Robinson and Brock Bowers as your top two assets is genuinely exciting, but the QB room of Jordan Love, C.J. Stroud, and Geno Smith looks like a support group for quarterbacks who peaked too soon. The good news: nchernandez just absolutely pillaged GiantHawkTua in back-to-back trades, walking away with multiple 2029 firsts and Jameson Williams while sending out scraps. Six first-round picks gives this rebuild a real runway, and if Love or Stroud rediscovers their form, this could jump into contention fast. Right now though, the WR depth outside of Marvin Harrison is genuinely thin.

Justin Jefferson and CeeDee Lamb are a top-5 WR duo in dynasty, full stop — but everything else on this roster screams 'I'm trying to win the Super Bowl with two stud WRs and hope.' The RB room of Chase Brown, Christian McCaffrey (on his last legs), and Saquon Barkley is a ticking time bomb of age and injury risk. Brock Purdy, Jared Goff, and Sam Darnold at QB is the most medium-quarterback energy possible, and the TE depth of Brenton Strange and Cade Otton should be illegal to write in the same sentence as Jefferson and Lamb. One first-round pick and a trade history of small losses suggests this window is closing faster than the owner realizes.

Lamar Jackson AND Patrick Mahomes at QB is an incredible luxury — and also a little insane when you consider neither will be elite dynasty assets in four years. Zero draft picks owned and no picks in the bank means when this window slams shut, it's going to be an ugly rebuild with nothing to show for it. The RB room of Derrick Henry, Josh Jacobs, and Tony Pollard is basically a retirement home with better cleats, and Travis Kelce showing up as a 'Short-term Production' TE tells you everything you need to know about this roster's long-term viability. This team needs to win it all in the next year or two, because the post-Lamar/Mahomes era is going to be a crater.

Let me get this straight — you traded Ja'Marr Chase, one of the most valuable players in dynasty football, and the best you could do was Ladd McConkey and some picks? And then you turned around and traded McConkey for Jalen Coker and a third? That is two consecutive trades that should be framed and hung in a museum of dynasty regrets. Malik Nabers is a legitimate cornerstone and Fernando Mendoza is an interesting dart throw, but the rest of this roster — Bhayshul Tuten, Quentin Johnston, Dak Prescott — reads like a waiver wire fire sale. Seven first-round picks is the only thing keeping this team from complete and total despair, but they need to stop trading them away for veterans on the wrong side of 30.

Five first-round picks and a roster headlined by George Pickens, TreVeyon Henderson, Jadarian Price, and Tyler Shough — which sounds exciting until you remember those are all either injury risks, depth chart questions, or guys who haven't proven a single thing in the NFL. The QB room of Tyler Shough, Aaron Rodgers, and Quinn Ewers is a monument to hopeful speculation, and George Kittle as your top TE is a short-term band-aid on a gaping dynasty wound. Seth has been winning trades on paper — flipping Gibbs back to ekleiner for a massive pick haul was actually smart — but the raw talent floor here is so low that 'rebuild' is doing a lot of heavy lifting. This team is picks and prayers, and we'll check back in 2028.
